WCET Builds the Case for Its Combined Value

WCET asked Ricochet to redesign its brand architecture so both of its member groups can see why a combined membership is worth keeping.

What was holding WCET back?

WCET, the technology-focused membership program of the Western Interstate Commission for Higher Education, serves more than 400 member organizations. Its members fall into two distinct groups of higher education professionals whose needs don't always overlap. As college and university budgets tighten, every membership faces closer review. WCET needed a clear way to show both audiences why the combined membership is worth keeping, and its brand was not making that case on its own.

What did Ricochet build?

Ricochet is leading a full brand architecture redesign that reaches into member benefits and product consolidation. The work draws on WCET's current messaging, collateral, member journey and competitive landscape. Ricochet is reviewing WCET's brand standards against its January 2026 visual refresh to set new visual design standards. The team is also documenting the member benefits available at each membership tier. Every piece is planned with future AI-assisted marketing collateral in mind.

What changed for WCET's members?

The work is still in progress, so results are not in yet. The goal is a clear, tested way for WCET to explain the value of belonging to both sides of its membership. When the redesign is complete, members in each group should be able to see which benefits come with their tier and why the combined membership serves them. That message will rest on research rather than assumption.

CMS Modernizes Its Marketing Technology

Ricochet led the Colorado Medical Society's full HubSpot Marketing Hub implementation, completing more than 100 configuration tasks and training staff for the switch.

What was holding CMS back?

The Colorado Medical Society (CMS) serves more than 6,000 members across all specialties and employment settings. Its marketing and membership communications needed a true home. CMS was also running an AMS implementation at the same time, so any new marketing system had to fit alongside that project and start with clean records. CMS turned to Ricochet to lead a full HubSpot Marketing Hub implementation.

What did Ricochet build?

Ricochet completed over 100 general and specific configuration tasks to build CMS's new HubSpot instance to spec. The team prepared integration documentation and coordinated with the integration developer while the AMS project ran in parallel. Before launch, Ricochet refreshed CMS's email templates with HubSpot's newer cloning tools and set up a starting set of automations. A data cleanup meant the new system began with clean records. Staff trained through weekly on-demand assignments plus live in-person sessions.

What changed for CMS's members?

CMS targeted a partial launch by Labor Day and a full launch by Halloween, with time set aside afterward to resolve bugs. Members now hear from CMS through refreshed email templates and automations built on clean records. Ricochet continues to provide HubSpot Evolution Coaching, which keeps CMS staff confident and current as they put the new system to work for the physicians they serve.

NCAN’s Strategic Pivot to a Sustainable Membership Model

Ricochet helped NCAN rethink its membership model, using stakeholder interviews and member data to build a phased strategy that balances inclusivity with financial resilience.

What was holding NCAN back?

The National College Attainment Network (NCAN) works to close equity gaps in postsecondary attainment and has nearly 600 member organizations. Its mission was more critical than ever, but its membership structure had not kept pace. To scale its impact, NCAN needed a more sustainable, value-driven strategy that served the diverse needs of a growing network. That meant more than adjusting dues. NCAN wanted to rethink why organizations join and how membership works.

What did Ricochet build?

Ricochet started with a discovery phase built on in-depth stakeholder interviews and a close analysis of NCAN's member data and financial trends. Ricochet then led workshops with NCAN leadership to define core value propositions and find untapped growth opportunities. The result was a multi-phased Membership Model Strategy. Its roadmap gives NCAN data-backed recommendations on tiered pricing and enhanced member benefits, along with streamlined operating processes.

What changed for NCAN's members?

The new model ties membership directly to NCAN's strategic priorities. Tiered pricing gives organizations with diverse needs a fitting place in the network, and enhanced benefits give them clearer reasons to stay engaged. The framework balances mission-driven inclusivity with the financial resilience NCAN needs to lead the college attainment field for years to come, so members can count on a network built to last.

CoreNet Global Expands Through Paid Media

After cleaning CoreNet Global's data and growing its target audience by 25 percent, Ricochet ran paid media that beat the association's recruitment goals.

What was holding CoreNet Global back?

CoreNet Global serves nearly 10,000 members in 50 countries and is a leader in the corporate real estate field. Its traditional recruitment methods needed a modern spark. Growth depended on reaching industry leaders where they spend their time online, and that called for a cleaner audience list and a sharper digital presence. CoreNet Global teamed up with Ricochet to overhaul its digital recruitment.

What did Ricochet build?

Ricochet began with list hygiene, scrubbing outdated information and adding data to expand CoreNet Global's target audience by 25 percent. With a clean foundation in place, the team balanced one master budget across LinkedIn, Reddit, Meta and AdRoll. Ricochet produced banner ads along with personalized weekly emails written for specific member personas. Each month the team held an optimization sprint, using real-time reporting to shift tactics and get the most from every dollar.

What changed for CoreNet Global's members?

Prospective members now see CoreNet Global's message on the channels they already use, and the emails they receive speak to their own persona rather than a generic audience. Because the team adjusts campaigns every month, outreach stays current instead of going stale. The program beat CoreNet Global's recruitment goals, which means more corporate real estate professionals are joining the community.

NJCPA Transitions to HubSpot to Power Multichannel Communications

Ricochet guided NJCPA's move from Adestra to HubSpot on a strictly defined schedule and budget, training staff for nearly four months so they could run the platform themselves.

What was holding NJCPA back?

The New Jersey Society of Certified Public Accountants (NJCPA) serves nearly 13,000 members, and its email ran on Adestra. NJCPA wanted one unified marketing engine across many channels, which meant a complex move to HubSpot. The project called for enterprise-level configuration and AMS data integration project management, and staff needed training to run it. All of it had to happen on a strictly defined schedule and budget. NJCPA asked Ricochet to lead the effort.

What did Ricochet build?

Ricochet ran the project on a fixed schedule, opening with a Kickoff Workshop to align the teams and holding weekly status meetings throughout. Over nearly four months of weekly training sessions, Ricochet also delivered data integration mapping and HubSpot systems configuration. The team planned a communication preference center and gave guidance on email templates. NJCPA staff then built their own email templates and forms, along with the workflows behind them, taking ownership of the new platform.

What changed for NJCPA's members?

NJCPA members now hear from their society through far more than email. HubSpot powers texts, landing pages, social posts, ringless voicemail, online media and on-demand postcards. Ricochet also planned a communication preference center so members can have a say in what they receive. Because NJCPA staff build their own templates and workflows, they can respond to member needs without waiting on outside help.

NCADA Transforms a Pivotal Turning Point into a Growth Opportunity

After more than a decade of membership decline, NCADA worked with Ricochet on member research and audits that produced a Membership Growth Strategy with a five-year financial projection.

What was holding NCADA back?

The North Carolina Association of Defense Attorneys (NCADA) represents more than 800 attorneys and paralegals. For more than a decade, its membership had declined as traditional insurance defense work became a commodity. Business litigation opportunities were growing, but competition for member attention had never been higher. NCADA needed more than a quick fix. It needed a full strategic repositioning, so it partnered with Ricochet to find out what its members needed.

What did Ricochet build?

FelineVMA's Digital Transformation

Ricochet gave the Feline Veterinary Medical Association a digital strategy and five-year roadmap, built on member research, then led the search for its website redesign agency.

What was holding FelineVMA back?

The Feline Veterinary Medical Association (FelineVMA), formerly the American Association of Feline Practitioners, was ready to modernize its digital technology. It wanted a better experience for members, starting with a complete website redesign. A project that large needed a clear picture of what members wanted and what the current systems could do. FelineVMA turned to Ricochet to build that picture and plan the way forward.

What did Ricochet build?

Ricochet ran a member survey that drew more than a thousand responses and held focus groups with members and prospects. It interviewed stakeholders and audited the existing digital infrastructure and content, while organizing demos with digital solution providers. From that work came a Digital Strategy and a five-year Digital Roadmap. Ricochet then led agency selection for the website redesign, from writing the RFP through coordinating the final choice.

What changed for FelineVMA's members?

Members shaped FelineVMA's digital plans through a survey with more than a thousand responses, and members and prospects added detail in focus groups. The five-year roadmap turns that input into a steady path for improving the member experience. The website redesign, handled by an agency chosen through a careful process, gives members a modern site built around what they said they need.
